title: qochey as a common-property computation with shared result obligations
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A relation hypothesis makes qochey compute the properties shared by two complete descriptions rather than carry one fixed HOT/DRY/stage value. Its output must constrain a later result reference throughout a passage. The three conflicting GDT748 frames motivate the distinction but do not establish operand grouping or a written result.

design.access: Existing primary reports and their already exposed derived readings only. No raw target corpus, image, new admission, reserve, external contact or current qoqokeey/repetition experiment inspected. No target test or decoder built.
design.claim_ceiling: All semantic values are provisional hypotheses. Zero confirmed words. Structural composition, spaces, whole-form residuals and entry effects constrain a future shared writer but do not identify its meanings. This is raw retention, not experimental selection.
design.retained_stops: GDT913/914/915/916/925/928/930/947/949/970/979/980 and GDT981 remain unchanged. No universal adjacency agreement, source-copy sequence, free automaton, per-token gloss, arbitrary filler or new allomorphic exception is licensed.
design.navigation: Current route and composition context read. Bounded ideas search, ideas duplicates and route-check used as navigation; returned claim-bearing primaries read where named below. Search absence is not proof of novelty. Later queries were blocked by concurrently stale EXPERIMENT_INDEX.tsv; no refresh performed.

target_nomination.ownership: These strings are reproduced in GDT747/748 primary reports, not newly extracted. The last eight groups of f104v.23 remain unread; no complete line translation is claimed.

design.mechanism: Descriptions denote partial assignments on three finite axes. A binary common-property operation retains a coordinate exactly when both operands explicitly agree there; disagreement or absence yields unspecified. It neither copies the nearest property nor unites incompatible values. The computed bundle becomes a referable result and cannot acquire a later property absent from the common output without an independently written operation.

prospective_finite_semantics.domain: Three coordinates, each with values {0,1,unspecified}; 27 possible bundles. HOT/COLD, DRY/MOIST and MIDDLE/END are inherited guesses illustrating axes, not verified scientific labels.
prospective_finite_semantics.operation: meet(a,b)[j] = a[j] when a[j]=b[j] and a[j] is specified; unspecified otherwise.
prospective_finite_semantics.minimal_writer: Two globally licensed binary constructions: B B qochey and B qochey B. B denotes a complete description under one shared lexicon/grammar, not an arbitrary neighboring word. Both constructions have the same output semantics. No free arity, no result-specific meaning and no per-occurrence choice of which properties survive.
prospective_finite_semantics.composition_debt: The bundle writer, constituent boundaries, reference spelling and result attachment remain unselected. Both operator placements are declared in advance, but deciding whether a whole group is B still requires one finite shared grammar. No claim that q/o/chey individually means anything.

contrasting_rivals: Fixed DRY/MIDDLE predicts the same bundle in every context.
Nearest-bundle copying would add HOT in the nominated postfix frame.
Conjunction of both full bundles would demand both HOT and COLD.
worked_hypothetical_example.additional_frame_outputs: Using only the old GDT748 bundle hypotheses, the two other listed frames would return HOT/END and END respectively. These are not three independent confirmations: the operands and axes were selected by the older exploratory analysis.

design.actual_new_consequence: A later written predicate or reference to the common result must be true of both operands on the retained axes. For a mismatching axis it may not inherit just one operand. One globally owned result expression must recur consistently across differing pairs, including pairs that yield the same result. Merely observing a plausible qochey neighborhood would not test this consequence.
design.order_and_scope: The operation is commutative, so swapping its two genuine operands preserves the result; moving an operand across a constituent boundary can change it. Order is therefore used to recover grouping, not to invent directed thermal changes. The two surface placements alone are not a semantic success.
predecessor_review: GDT747 full-line report gives the initial opposite-temperature/shared-DRY-MIDDLE frame; its old fixed-value proposal is not accepted as an input fact.
GDT748 reports no repeated qochey consensus and poor unconditional neighborhood transfer (189/429, including 106 opposite-axis assignments). This candidate does not promote that transfer rule.
GDT750 gives qochey no active outside host and zero new cards under the global expansion. This remains a missing binding, not a newly passed relation.

IDEA065 inheritance and generic IDEA103 intersection concern different mechanisms: here the proposed written operator computes a two-operand result. That difference is provisional until result ownership is supplied.
likely_failure: No written result or common subject is currently owned; the hypothesis could amount only to a conventional renaming of an observed formal relation.
Allowing arbitrary operands or arbitrary result-reference labels would make the rule freely satisfiable and must be rejected.
The old axes may be wrong altogether, and the two surface placements may be unlicensed.
A complete passage may expose incompatible result predicates or require more operands than the fixed binary syntax.
The whole-form writer must pay for residuals and entry effects without glossing each remaining word independently.
design.smallest_useful_next_step: Before any decoder, inspect the already admitted complete occurrences for one prospectively fixed shared operand/result grammar that reads an entire nominated passage and yields an explicit result contrast. If no result is owned, retain RAW status rather than score neighborhood agreement.
